lab.title: Optional manual rehearsal: one small app, one slot and one tested restore
lab.purpose: Observe the difference between a plan, an app, a release swap and a restore using disposable school-themed content. This is optional practice, not an instruction for the course software to deploy resources.
prerequisites: An approved practice subscription with sufficient resource-creation permissions and available Linux Standard S1 capacity in the chosen region.
An approved small non-sensitive web artifact with visibly different build 12 and build 13 pages, and an authorized deployment process already understood by the learner.
A dedicated practice resource group and a recorded list of resources owned by this exercise; do not use a production plan or real pupil data.
A same-subscription practice storage account and container supporting the required SAS-based App Service backup authorization.
If practising private backup routing, an approved same-region VNet integration subnet, correct private DNS and storage network access; otherwise use the simpler approved reachable-storage scenario.
Permission from the cost owner and a planned end time. A custom-domain extension additionally requires control of an unused real DNS name and an appropriate certificate.
lab.costWarning: Standard workers are billed while allocated even if the app is stopped. A staging slot shares that capacity but can increase load. Storage, retained manual backups, monitoring, private endpoints, VPN and data transfer can add charges. Do not upgrade to Premium or create private-network infrastructure merely to finish this small lab. Budget alerts are notifications, not an automatic spending stop.
steps: Record the chosen names, region and estimated charges. Create a dedicated Linux Standard S1 plan and a compatible Web App using the portal flow taught in the first lesson.
Deploy build 12 using the approved deployment process. Browse the default domain copied from Overview and record the visible build and a successful request.

Create staging under Deployment slots, inspect the cloned configuration, restrict its access appropriately, and deploy build 13. Verify that its separate URL shows build 13 while production still shows build 12.
Add a harmless environment-name setting with different values for production and staging and mark it as a deployment slot setting. Have the practice artifact show only this nonsecret value.
Review Swap with staging as source and production as target. Perform an ordinary manual swap, then verify that production shows build 13 while retaining its production environment value.
Reverse the swap and verify that build 12 returns. Record that this experiment changed application content, not an external database or document archive.

Configure custom backups to the practice container with a six-hour schedule and explicit seven-day scheduled retention. If using the private scenario, verify and enable backup over VNet integration for the relevant slot.
Run one manual backup, inspect its success status and corresponding ZIP and XML artifacts, and record that this manual recovery point has indefinite retention.

Restore the chosen backup into an isolated same-OS test target or the disposable staging slot after confirming its contents may be overwritten. Observe target interruption and then test the restored page and configuration.

Optionally map an unused real subdomain with the displayed CNAME and verification TXT, bind an eligible certificate with SNI and inspect the browser certificate. Skip this extension if you lack domain ownership or a safe certificate plan.
expectedResults: The app and plan appear as separate resources, and the slot shares the existing plan rather than creating dedicated workers.
The swap exchanges visible builds while the marked environment value stays associated with its final slot.
A successful custom backup produces identifiable artifacts, and a tested restore reproduces the intended supported content in the chosen target.
Any missing identity, network, authentication or TLS configuration is identified explicitly instead of being assumed restored.
If the domain extension is performed, public DNS, app hostname recognition and the browser's certificate all match the intended custom name.
cleanup: Remove only the lab's scheduled backup configuration and lab-owned manual backup artifacts after the rehearsal has been recorded and the cost owner confirms they are no longer needed.
If a lab-only custom name was added, remove its routing record and binding deliberately so no dangling CNAME remains. Preserve shared certificates and unrelated DNS records.
Disconnect lab VNet integration before removing its network resources. Delete only lab-owned private endpoints and DNS records, leaving pre-existing office and shared network resources intact.
Delete the lab app, slots and isolated restore target, then delete the paid plan only after verifying that no other app uses it.
Delete a resource group only if its inventory contains exclusively disposable lab resources. Recheck the recorded plan, storage and monitoring resources for remaining charges.
